'''Claude Lemaréchal''' is a French [[applied mathematician]], and former senior researcher (''directeur de recherche'') at [[INRIA]]<ref>INRIA is the acronym for the [[National Institute for Research in Computer Science and Control]], in the original French, ''Institut national de recherche en informatique et en automatique'' (INRIA).</ref> near [[Grenoble]], France.

In [[mathematical optimization]], Claude Lemaréchal is known for his work in [[iterative method|numerical methods]] for  [[nonlinear optimization]], especially for problems with [[subdifferential|nondifferentiable kinks]]. Lemaréchal and [[Philip Wolfe (mathematician)|Philip Wolfe]] pioneered [[bundle method]]s of descent for [[convex minimization]].<ref name="Citation of Claude Lemaréchal">[http://www.mathprog.org/Old-Optima-Issues/optima44.pdf Citation of Claude Lemaréchal] for the [[George Dantzig]] Prize in 1994 in ''Optima'', Issue 44 (1994) pages 4-5.</ref>

== Awards ==

In 1994, Claude Lemaréchal and [[Roger J-B Wets]] were each awarded the [[George B. Dantzig]] Prize. Recognizing "original research that has had a major impact on the field of mathematical programming", the Dantzig Prize is awarded by the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM) and the Mathematical Programming Society (MPS).<ref name="Citation of Claude Lemaréchal"/>

==Lagrangian duality and nonconvex primal problems==
{{See also|Lagrangian multiplier|Convex analysis|Convex optimization}}
Soon after joining [[National Institute for Research in Computer Science and Control|INRIA]] (then named "[[National Institute for Research in Computer Science and Control|IRIA]]"), Lemaréchal had the assignment of helping a glass-manufacturer with a problem of [[scheduling (production processes)|scheduling its production]], a problem whose first formulation required [[optimization|minimizing]] a [[convex function|non-convex function]]. For this non-convex minimization problem, Lemaréchal applied the theory of [[Lagrangian multiplier|Lagrangian duality]] that was described in Lasdon's ''Optimization Theory for Large Systems''.<ref>
* {{cite book|last=Lasdon|first=Leon&nbsp;S.|title=Optimization theory for large systems|publisher=The Macmillan Company|series=Macmillan series in operations research|location=New York|year=1970|pages=xi+523|mr=337317}}
* {{cite book|last=Lasdon|first=Leon&nbsp;S.|title=Optimization theory for large systems|publisher=Dover Publications, Inc.|location=Mineola, New York|year=2002|edition=reprint of the 1970 Macmillan|pages=xiii+523|mr=1888251}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
|first=Karen
|last=Aardal|authorlink=Karen Aardal
|title=''Optima'' interview Claude Lemaréchal
|journal=Optima: Mathematical Programming Society Newsletter
|pages=2–4
|date=March 1995
|url =http://www.mathprog.org/Old-Optima-Issues/optima45.pdf
}}</ref> Because the primal problem was non-convex, there was no guarantee that a solution to the dual problem would provide useful information about the primal. Nonetheless, the dual problem did furnish useful information.<ref>
*{{Cite report|last=Lemaréchal|first=Claude|title=Utilisation de la dualité dans les problémes non&nbsp;convexes [Use of duality for non-convex problems]|date=April 1973|issue=16|location=Domaine de&nbsp;Voluceau, [[Rocquencourt, Yvelines|Rocquencourt]],&nbsp;78150 [[Le Chesnay|Le&nbsp;Chesnay]], France|publisher=[[INRIA|IRIA]] (Laboratoire de recherche en informatique et automatique)|pages=41|authorlink=Claude Lemaréchal}}<!-- Ekeland cites this report in the [[Comptes Rendus|CRAS]] announcement of the results of his Appendix&nbsp;I -->

**{{cite book|last1=Hiriart-Urruty|first1=Jean-Baptiste|last2=Lemaréchal|first2=Claude|chapter=XII&nbsp;Abstract duality for practitioners|title=Convex analysis and minimization algorithms, Volume&nbsp;II: Advanced theory and bundle methods|series=Grundlehren der Mathematischen Wissenschaften [Fundamental Principles of Mathematical Sciences]|volume=306|publisher=Springer-Verlag|location=Berlin|year=1993|pages=136–193 (and Bibliographical comments on pp.&nbsp;334–335)|isbn=978-3-540-56852-0|mr=1295240 }}
</ref> Lemaréchal's success with [[Lagrangian multiplier|Lagrangian dual]] [[subgradient method|methods]] on [[nonlinear programming]] problems with [[convex function|nonconvexities]] interested Ivar Ekeland and Jean–Pierre Aubin, who applied the [[Shapley–Folkman lemma]] to explain Lemaréchal's success.<ref>{{Cite journal

* Page 373: {{cite book|last=Ekeland|first=Ivar|chapter = Appendix&nbsp;I: An ''a&nbsp;priori'' estimate in convex programming|editor=Ekeland, Ivar |editor2=Temam, Roger|title=Convex analysis and variational problems|edition=translated, with new appendices, from the (1973) French|series=Studies in mathematics and its applications|volume=1|publisher=North-Holland Publishing Co.|location=Amsterdam|year=1976|pages=357–373|mr=463994}}

</ref> The Aubin–Ekeland analysis of duality gaps  considered the ''[[Convex conjugate#Biconjugate convex|convex]]'' [[Convex conjugate#Biconjugate|closure]] of a nonconvex minimization problem — that is, the problem defined by the [[Kuratowski closure axioms|closed]] [[convex hull|convex]] [[closure operator|hull]] of the [[epigraph (mathematics)|epigraph]] of the original problem. Following Ekeland and Aubin, similar applications of the [[Shapley–Folkman lemma]] are described in optimization monographs<ref name="Ekeland" /><ref>

==Bundle methods of descent==
{{See also|Convex optimization|Subgradient method}}
Lemaréchal's research also led to his work on ([[nonlinear conjugate gradient method|conjugate]]) [[subgradient method]]s and on bundle methods of [[gradient descent|descent]] for [[convex optimization|convex minimization problems]].
